analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-free caused by double-destruction of the same decoder list pointer. The harness allocates `list` and passes it as the `decoders` argument to `flb_parser_create()`. On parser creation failure, `flb_parser_create`/`flb_parser_destroy` frees `parser->decoders` via `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy` (free at flb_parser_decoder.c:772). The harness then enters its `fuzz_parser == NULL` cleanup path and calls `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy(list)` again, which iterates/frees already-freed memory, triggering UAF in `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy` (read at line 754).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Input must drive the fuzzer to create a non-NULL `list` (decoders enabled) and make `flb_parser_create` fail after taking ownership of that list (so internal destroy path frees it). Then `fuzz_parser` is NULL, causing the harness’s fallback cleanup to call `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy(list)` a second time. Data flow: fuzz input -> parser_fuzzer builds `list` -> passes to `flb_parser_create` -> failure path frees list internally -> harness else-branch frees same list again.
